title: The Political Legacy of American Slavery

original_reference.notes: The original paper reports -0.127 (0.043), using classical homoskedastic weighted-OLS standard errors. The supplied regression preserves the original coefficient, standard error, controls, weights and sample. Standard errors are not clustered by state.

sample_notes: The unchanged original CSV contains 2,931 counties; the authors' 14-state restriction leaves 1,329 before complete-case filtering.
Applying the original logarithms and squares, then requiring finite original regressors, outcome and exposure and positive weights, yields the same 1,152 counties as Table 1, column 2.
One row represents one county. Historical values are already interpolated to 2000 county boundaries; students do not need to merge historical maps or reshape panel data.
The supplied controls are exactly the original 14 substantive regression terms, including the original latitude and longitude squares. No contemporary mediator or cotton instrument has been added.
The 13 state indicators omit AL; include an intercept. The original sample.size weights are retained without rounding.
The regression coefficient and classical weighted-OLS standard error reproduce the authors' published specification.
identification_notes: This is the paper's conditional county-level association, not its separate instrumental-variable analysis. The OLS estimate alone does not establish a causal effect of slavery.
Some 1860 economic controls may themselves reflect slavery; the original adjustment set does not establish that every variable is a causally appropriate control.

The outcome concerns white respondents and includes Democratic leaners. A ten-percentage-point exposure increase implies 10 times the raw coefficient in percentage points of Democratic identification.
Reported standard errors follow the original classical weighted-OLS convention; they are not clustered by state or adjusted for cross-county spatial dependence.

provenance.author_script: slavery-jop-replication.R, base1860.form and the county Table 1 models
provenance.transformations: Apply the authors' 14-state restriction, four logarithms and two geographic squares; retain the original complete cases and weights; sort by county FIPS and supply state indicators with AL omitted.
